evals.prompt: The same user id string '12345' shows up on my WhatsApp inbox and two Instagram accounts. Will their Redis state collide?
evals.expected_output: No: Wappa scopes caches by InboxRef.cache_namespace + user_id; use self.cache_factory (already bound) or create_cache_factory(...)(inbox_id=inbox_ref.cache_namespace, user_id=...); never hand-build keys; a host link between identities is host-owned evidence.

evals.prompt: What happens to my flow state when the TTL expires or Redis is down?
evals.expected_output: get returns None on miss/expiry and the flow must treat it as 'no active flow' (restart or explain); upsert takes ttl seconds and renew_ttl extends; outages raise and should fail the handler visibly rather than silently resetting; memory backend loses state on restart.
assertions: outage is not silently treated as empty

evals.prompt: Can I store the customer's submitted form and the Instagram access token in the state cache so my AI tool can read them?
evals.expected_output: Workflow state holds only transient flow data; submitted business records belong in host persistence (DB or a Table Cache you own) and credentials never go into caches or tool arguments — trusted adapters resolve them per operation via InboxCredentialAccess.
assertions: does not hand credentials to tools
points business records to host persistence

evals.prompt: Where should I keep the message IDs of my sends and the user's Instagram username so I can use them later?
evals.expected_output: Profile facts (from resolve_platform_user_profile) go in the Host's User record or the per-User user cache scoped by Inbox; message IDs for status correlation go in host persistence keyed by InboxRef and message_id (state cache only for in-flight flow needs, with a TTL); never hand-built keys; the same IGSID on two Inboxes is two Users.
assertions: keys data by Inbox and User, not a raw global ID
uses create_user_cache or host persistence, no hand-built keys
keeps durable correlation out of TTL-only flow state

evals.prompt: Save every completed intake to Postgres from my Wappa handler and read them back for an admin page.
evals.expected_output: Adds PostgresDatabasePlugin(url=os.environ['DATABASE_URL'], models=[...], auto_create_tables=False for production); writes with `async with self.db() as session`, reads with self.db_read(); uses session.execute not .exec; keys rows by Inbox and User; does not keep submissions only in a cache.
assertions: uses PostgresDatabasePlugin with an explicit url
calls self.db() as an async context manager
rows carry the Inbox identity, not only user_id

evals.prompt: Turn on Redis for my Wappa app and send a follow-up if the user goes silent for 15 minutes.
evals.expected_output: Wappa(cache='redis') with REDIS_URL (no second RedisPlugin); ExpiryPlugin plus a module-level @expiry_registry.on_expire_action handler; arms it with create_expiry_cache().set(action, user_id, 900) and re-arms on each message; parses the InboxRef from the key and uses create_expiry_messenger; mentions keyspace notifications and idempotency across workers; no CronPlugin for a per-User timer.
assertions: uses Wappa(cache="redis") without adding RedisPlugin again
does not use a cron for a per-User timer
